raw_case_text:
A 77-year-old man presented with depressive mood, asthenia, anorexia and weight loss of 20 kg. He also had a 1-month history of an enlarging and non-painful breast lump (Fig. 1). He did not have fever, night sweats, cough or breathlessness. He denied trauma or contact with tuberculosis. Physical examination revealed a firm and elastic mass in the internal quadrants of the left breast with well-defined contours, about 6 cm in diameter. Local temperature was normal and the overlying skin and nipple were intact. There was no evident neck or axillary palpable adenopathy. Laboratory tests showed a white blood cell count within normal limits, haemoglobin of 12.1 g/dl and C-reactive protein of 5.42 mg/dl; all other blood chemistry results were within normal limits. Radiography showed no obvious lesions (Fig. 2). Mammary ultrasound revealed in the inner quadrants of the left breast a thick-walled cystic formation measuring 69x20 mm, with detritus in the region of greatest slope. Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of a white fluid revealed a necrotic background with granulomas without neoplastic cells. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and acid-fast bacilli stain of the aspirate were both positive for tuberculosis. Computed tomography (CT) of the thorax showed a liquid collection in the left anterior thoracic wall, measuring 31x80 mm, associated with irregularity and discontinuity of the 4th left costal cartilage, with a fistulous tract that crossed the cartilage into a small locus posterior to the left internal mammary artery; in the upper left lobe there was a cavitated nodule measuring 22 mm, compatible with an active tuberculous process (Figs. 3 and 4). Positron emission tomography (PET) showed a possible nodule in the left upper lobe and bilateral mediastinum-hilar adenopathy, with increased uptake of FDG-F18 (Fig. 5).
Peripheral uptake of FDG-F18 was noted as well in a hypodense mass in the left anterior thoracic wall. An interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) was positive and HIV serology was negative. A sputum smear was positive for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) which was also positive by Ziehl-Neelsen staining. Sputum culture was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex that was sensitive to all tested drugs. The final diagnosis was pulmonary tuberculosis (PT) with a tuberculous mass in the left anterior chest wall, as a result of direct extension from underlying pleural and pulmonary disease.
Quadruple therapy with anti-tuberculosis drugs was started: isoniazid (300 mg), rifampicin (450 mg), ethambutol (800 mg) and pyrazinamide (1500 mg). The mass did not improve with medical treatment and so was drained. The patient was discharged home following 26 days in hospital after he had improved clinically, gained weight, and three sputum smears were negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 77-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of an enlarging painless left breast lump accompanied by depressed mood, asthenia, anorexia, and a 20 kg weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the month prior to presentation, the patient noticed a progressively enlarging painless mass in the inner quadrants of his left breast in the setting of profound constitutional decline (20 kg weight loss, anorexia, asthenia, and depressed mood).
subjective.past_medical_history: Denied chest trauma or known contact with tuberculosis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for painless left breast mass, asthenia, anorexia, depressed mood, and 20 kg weight loss; negative for fever, night sweats, cough, or breathlessness.

objective.physical_examination: A well-defined, firm, elastic 6 cm mass in the medial quadrants of the left breast with normal local skin temperature, intact overlying skin and nipple, and no palpable cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Normal WBC count, Hb 12.1 g/dL, CRP 5.42 mg/dL, normal blood chemistry, positive IGRA, and negative HIV serology. Plain chest radiograph was unremarkable. Breast ultrasound showed a 69 × 20 mm thick-walled cystic collection with dependent debris in the medial left breast.
objective.advanced_workup: Thoracic CT demonstrated a 31 × 80 mm left anterior chest wall fluid collection eroding through the 4th left costal cartilage via a fistulous tract posterior to the left internal mammary artery, plus a 22 mm cavitary nodule in the left upper lung lobe. 18F-FDG PET-CT showed hypermetabolic uptake in the left upper lobe nodule, bilateral hilar/mediastinal lymph nodes, and the rim of the left anterior thoracic wall mass. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of white fluid from the breast mass showed necrotic granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Left breast/chest wall aspirate AFB stain and M. tuberculosis PCR, sputum Ziehl-Neelsen smear, and pan-sensitive sputum Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex culture were all positive, confirming cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis with direct trans-pleural/costal cartilage extension (empyema necessitatis / retromammary cold abscess) presenting as a male breast mass. He was treated with quadruple anti-TB therapy (isoniazid 300 mg, rifampicin 450 mg, ethambutol 800 mg, pyrazinamide 1500 mg) and percutaneous/surgical drainage of the breast collection, achieving 3 negative sputum smears, weight gain, and hospital discharge on day 26.
